small_guidance:
- The conv (torch cuDNN) likely dominates runtime now; tuning the fused GN+scale+maxpool+clamp kernel further has limited headroom. Still, try adding autotune configs with BLOCK_OH=32/BLOCK_OW=32 num_warps=4 and BLOCK_OH=16/BLOCK_OW=64, since H_out=W_out=63 (post-pool 31) — coverage with fewer programs may help.
- Merge `_gn_stats_kernel` into a single persistent kernel: launch one program per `(N, G)`, compute mean/rstd, then in the same program loop over channels-in-group and output tiles applying scale+maxpool+clamp — eliminates the separate stats launch and the mean/rstd global round-trip.
- Pass `clamp_min`/`clamp_max` as `tl.constexpr` floats so they bake into PTX; also pass `H`, `W`, `H_out`, `W_out`, `P` as constexpr since they are static across the run.
large_guidance:
- Replace the `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)` with implicit im2col gather. With in_channels=8, kernel=3 (K=72), out_channels=64, OH=OW=126, the GEMM is small-K and bandwidth-bound — a fused conv+GN-prep epilogue will beat cuDNN here and remove the dominant cost.
- Fuse the entire pipeline into two kernels: (1) conv → write conv output AND per-(N,G) partial sums for GN (using atomics or a two-stage reduction); (2) finalize GN stats and apply scale + 4×4 maxpool + clamp directly from the conv output. This eliminates a full read/write pass over the NCHW=128·64·126·126 tensor.
- Alternatively, use channels_last memory layout end-to-end so the per-channel scale/gamma/beta loads broadcast across a contiguous channel vector, and the maxpool window of 4×4 reads stay coalesced along W.
